purpose: Practical settlement-scale build language for all 24 archipelago civilizations. These rules translate regional history, architecture and culture into repeatable hamlets, villages, towns, cities, ports, fortresses, sacred sites, industrial districts and ruins without making settlements inside one region feel cloned.
global_rules: A settlement inherits the civilization's structural grammar first and its island function second. Function changes the expression; it does not replace the culture.
Hamlets are the most conservative and local. Capitals, ports and guild districts show the most imported ideas.
Every settlement needs one dominant circulation logic: road, stair, boardwalk, canal, quay, cavern bridge, causeway, platform or courtyard network.
Every settlement needs one ordinary civic focus: market, hall, well/cistern, dock, shrine, mill, station or commons. Signature monuments are optional and rare.
Production infrastructure must be embedded in inhabited space unless danger or scale provides a clear reason to isolate it.
At least one-third of any major settlement should be non-production space: homes, inns, gardens, shrines, civic buildings, storage, roads, parks, ruins or public waterfront.
Resource buildings must use local structural logic even when the machinery inside is standardized.
Border settlements may borrow one or two visible motifs from neighbors, but silhouette, circulation and ordinary housing remain locally recognizable.
Ruins preserve an older version of the same culture unless the site is explicitly pre-civilizational or foreign.
Do not make every island dense. Wilderness, agricultural space, water, cliffs, forest and empty approach routes are part of settlement design.

settlement_classes.hamlet: 3-8 primary buildings plus work structures; one local path/dock/boardwalk spine; no monumental civic building.
settlement_classes.village: 8-25 primary buildings; one recognizable civic focus; one or two specialized work areas; clear vernacular housing pattern.
settlement_classes.town: Multiple neighborhoods or work quarters; secondary streets/routes; dedicated civic, storage and hospitality functions.
settlement_classes.city: Distinct districts with different uses; major infrastructure; multiple public spaces; imported influences visible but locally translated.
settlement_classes.port: Settlement organized around transfer between land and water; warehouses, repair, lodging and navigation are mandatory even if trade is not the primary function.
settlement_classes.fortress: Defense controls circulation and sightlines. Civilian life, storage and water/food access must be designed as part of the fortress rather than added outside afterward.
settlement_classes.sacred_or_scholarly: Quiet circulation, processional movement, archives/gardens/courts/observatories or ritual landscape matter more than raw size.
settlement_classes.industrial: Separate dangerous process, logistics, storage, workers and civic life into readable zones while keeping the entire complex culturally coherent.
settlement_classes.ruin: Show original function and construction logic before damage. Ruins should reveal history, not just add random broken walls.

The Great Cold North.circulation: Protected footpaths between compounds, sled tracks and short covered connectors; settlements turn inward from wind.
The Great Cold North.hamlet: Two or three family compounds around a shared winter hall or animal shelter; stone plinths and very steep roofs dominate.
The Great Cold North.village: Several kin compounds orbit one large communal hall; storehouses and smokehouses form the protected downwind edge.
The Great Cold North.town_city: Rare and compact. A great hall complex, winter market, smith yard and harbor form one protected cluster surrounded by large empty landscape.
The Great Cold North.port: Low enclosed harbor, high-bow boathouses, heavy chain posts, beacon cairns and storage dug into slopes.
The Great Cold North.fortress: Broad, low earth-and-stone ramparts with timber fighting galleries; avoid elegant towers.
The Great Cold North.sacred: Cairn fields, standing stones, memorial posts and hall shrines integrated into landscape rather than separate temple precincts.
The Great Cold North.industrial: Ice, timber or preservation work is distributed among compounds; large industry should feel like an enlarged hall-yard system.
The Great Cold North.ruin: Massive stone foundations, fallen hall posts and weathered megaliths with little surviving delicate detail.
The Great Cold North.build_signature: Broad low silhouette + enormous roof + visible empty wilderness around settlement.

Frost Marches.circulation: Covered lanes, timber bridges, raised walks and enclosed yards.
Frost Marches.hamlet: Tight cluster of raised timber houses, barn, smokehouse and roadside shrine around a sheltered lane.
Frost Marches.village: Covered market street becomes the spine; workshops open directly onto it while farms sit outside a compact defensive edge.
Frost Marches.town_city: Bridge or crossing town with market hall, guild yard, fortified inn, watchtowers and a practical street grid adapted to snow.
Frost Marches.port: Timber quay behind a windbreak, warehouse sheds, ferry hall and compact inn quarter.
Frost Marches.fortress: Palisaded ridge or river fort with covered wall walks and refuge hall.
Frost Marches.sacred: Small refuge chapels, bell towers and travelers' shrines rather than monumental temples.
Frost Marches.industrial: Sawmills, winter storehouses and workshops stay attached to ordinary streets and yards.
Frost Marches.ruin: Collapsed palisades, abandoned bridge abutments and roofless frontier halls reclaimed by taiga.
Frost Marches.build_signature: Covered movement and compact repairable timber construction.

Shattered Ice Coast.circulation: Protected quay-to-yard routes, enclosed alleys and beacon-linked sea lanes.
Shattered Ice Coast.hamlet: Lee-cove fishing cluster with stone bases, heavy shutters, smokehouses and one rescue shed.
Shattered Ice Coast.village: Harbor-facing row settlement with repair yard, fish sheds, storm chapel and beacon.
Shattered Ice Coast.town_city: Enclosed harbor city with sea fort, salvage quarter, ship repair district and inner protected market.
Shattered Ice Coast.port: The port is the settlement: breakwater, covered dry dock, crane piers, rescue station and wreck yard define the plan.
Shattered Ice Coast.fortress: Sea keep integrated into breakwater and beacon network rather than inland castle.
Shattered Ice Coast.sacred: Storm chapels, memorial bells and cliff cemeteries oriented toward sea routes.
Shattered Ice Coast.industrial: Salvage, ice cutting and ship repair use low stone sheds and reusable ship timber; yards are wind-protected.
Shattered Ice Coast.ruin: Storm-broken piers, half-collapsed sea walls and wreck timber reused by later buildings.
Shattered Ice Coast.build_signature: Stone lower half + salvaged timber upper half + harbor engineering.

The Crownlands.circulation: Planned streets, formal gates, paved bridges, arcades and clear hierarchy from avenue to lane.
The Crownlands.hamlet: Ordered farmstead cluster around a small square, well and civic marker; even rural layouts show surveying.
The Crownlands.village: Market square, chapel/hall, straight primary street and defined plots with stone or half-timber houses.
The Crownlands.town_city: Districted planned city with civic square, guild streets, gardens, barracks, markets and formal gates.
The Crownlands.port: Regulated quay blocks, customs house, naval pier and aligned warehouses behind arcades.
The Crownlands.fortress: Geometric curtain walls, gatehouses, barracks courts and integrated civilian quarter.
The Crownlands.sacred: Formal cloisters, processional courts and institutional temples or abbeys.
The Crownlands.industrial: Workshops are zoned into orderly guild quarters with storage courts and service alleys.
The Crownlands.ruin: Readable street grids, broken arches and reused civic stone; later settlements often occupy old foundations.
The Crownlands.build_signature: Measured geometry and public order visible at every scale.

The High Kingdom.circulation: Switchback streets, monumental stairs, bridge crossings and stacked terraces.
The High Kingdom.hamlet: Stone houses cling to terraces around a spring, chapel or stair landing.
The High Kingdom.village: Vertical sequence of lower farms, middle market terrace and upper chapel/watch tower.
The High Kingdom.town_city: Stacked districts linked by stairs and bridges; palace/monastery/keep crowns the skyline.
The High Kingdom.port: Small but dramatic cliff harbor connected to upper settlement by lifts, stairs or switchbacks.
The High Kingdom.fortress: Bridge-castle, pass gate or ridge keep integrated directly into mountain movement.
The High Kingdom.sacred: Terraced monastery, hanging garden, observatory and pilgrimage stair.
The High Kingdom.industrial: Prestige masonry, bridge yards and workshops occupy terraces; bulk quarrying remains visually secondary.
The High Kingdom.ruin: Broken bridges, stairways leading to vanished terraces and isolated towers on inaccessible ridges.
The High Kingdom.build_signature: Vertical procession and architecture that appears to grow from cliffs.

The Hearthlands.circulation: Curving lanes, lakeside paths, covered bridges and village greens.
The Hearthlands.hamlet: Cottages, barn, kitchen garden and shared hearth/oven around a protected green.
The Hearthlands.village: Inn or market green becomes center; brewery, mill, pier and homes cluster within short walking distance.
The Hearthlands.town_city: Dense but low-rise lake town divided into inn, brewery, market, residential and waterfront quarters.
The Hearthlands.port: Ferry hall, covered pier, boathouses, waterside inn and modest cargo sheds.
The Hearthlands.fortress: Rare; usually a fortified manor, bridge gate or refuge hall rather than a military citadel.
The Hearthlands.sacred: Garden abbey, bell tower, orchard cloister and guesthouse integrated with village life.
The Hearthlands.industrial: Brewing, smoking, milling and food processing are embedded into ordinary neighborhoods.
The Hearthlands.ruin: Abandoned mills, manor foundations and overgrown garden walls rather than dramatic fortifications.
The Hearthlands.build_signature: Domestic warmth, walkability and buildings oriented toward gathering.

The Timberlands.circulation: Logging roads, river paths, log bridges and long workshop streets.
The Timberlands.hamlet: Forester cabins, drying sheds and one oversized shared timber frame in a clearing.
The Timberlands.village: Sawmill or river landing anchors settlement; homes and workshops sit under broad exposed-frame roofs.
The Timberlands.town_city: Guild hall, sawmill district, carpentry streets, log port and arboretum/green spaces form distinct quarters.
The Timberlands.port: Boom chains, log ponds, cranes, long timber warehouses and repair docks dominate the waterfront.
The Timberlands.fortress: Tall timber watch structures, palisades and earthworks; stone is used mainly for foundations and fire protection.
The Timberlands.sacred: Protected grove, foresters' lodge, seed archive and memorial trees rather than masonry temples.
The Timberlands.industrial: Production is visually celebrated: exposed joinery, water power, drying yards and stacked timber are part of the townscape.
The Timberlands.ruin: Rotting piers, mossed stone mill races and giant surviving frame posts swallowed by forest.
The Timberlands.build_signature: Structure itself is ornament: beams, braces and joinery stay visible.

The Breadbasket.circulation: Field roads, canal towpaths, lock crossings and straight farm lanes.
The Breadbasket.hamlet: Farm compounds with long barn, farmhouse, granary and irrigation ditch around working yards.
The Breadbasket.village: Mill, produce green and canal landing anchor clustered farmhouses and craft buildings.
The Breadbasket.town_city: Market town organized around canal basin, granary district, mill race and administrative water council.
The Breadbasket.port: Barge docks, grain warehouses, lock gates and weighing house; water movement matters more than seafaring aesthetics.
The Breadbasket.fortress: Low flood embankments, gatehouses and defended granaries rather than high walls.
The Breadbasket.sacred: Harvest shrines, orchard chapels and memorial groves embedded in working land.
The Breadbasket.industrial: Mills, compost/moss systems, storage and processing remain adjacent to fields and canals.
The Breadbasket.ruin: Dry canals, broken mill wheels, old field walls and abandoned granary foundations that still shape plots.
The Breadbasket.build_signature: Landscape engineering is architecture: canals, fields, barns and mills read as one system.

The Grand Exchange.circulation: Quays, arcades, warehouse lanes, bridges, service alleys and dense pedestrian markets.
The Grand Exchange.hamlet: Rare; small satellite dock settlement with inn, warehouse, counting office and mixed imported materials.
The Grand Exchange.village: Merchant quay town with market street, bonded storage and multilingual/foreign quarter cues.
The Grand Exchange.town_city: Dense district city: exchange, guild, customs, warehouse, residential, lodging and civic quarters all interlock.
The Grand Exchange.port: Layered quays, cranes, customs basins, bonded warehouses, pilot offices and foreign docks.
The Grand Exchange.fortress: Commercial defense: harbor chains, customs fort, protected treasury and watch towers rather than broad military occupation.
The Grand Exchange.sacred: Small imported faith houses and guild shrines share crowded blocks; no single religious style dominates.
The Grand Exchange.industrial: Sorting, storage and repacking dominate; primary production and most transformation stay in source regions.
The Grand Exchange.ruin: Burned warehouse shells, obsolete quays and old market arcades absorbed into new commercial blocks.
The Grand Exchange.build_signature: Density, mixed materials and visible movement of goods.

Engineer's Reach.circulation: Service roads, rail cuts, gantries, elevated walks and clear maintenance corridors.
Engineer's Reach.hamlet: Worker cottages and a compact workshop yard near one machine or utility installation.
Engineer's Reach.village: Workshop town with machine hall, parts stores, testing yard and communal canteen/market.
Engineer's Reach.town_city: District city divided into machine halls, rail works, laboratories, utilities, residences and civic demonstration spaces.
Engineer's Reach.port: Industrial transfer quay with cranes, standardized sheds and rail-to-ship loading.
Engineer's Reach.fortress: Infrastructure defense: controlled gates, redundant power, protected workshops and observation towers.
Engineer's Reach.sacred: Guild memorial halls, inventor monuments and demonstration galleries rather than traditional temples dominating skyline.
Engineer's Reach.industrial: Machinery is visible but housed in coherent brick/stone shells; utility corridors connect districts rather than one mega-building.
Engineer's Reach.ruin: Obsolete test rigs, abandoned viaducts and brick shells that reveal older technical generations.
Engineer's Reach.build_signature: Readable systems, modular bays and exposed movement of power/materials.

Artisan Coast.circulation: Courtyard lanes, arcaded streets, stepped coastal paths and workshop-front market routes.
Artisan Coast.hamlet: Small cluster of live-work houses around one shared kiln, dye yard or glass furnace courtyard.
Artisan Coast.village: Craft street with open workshops, colorful courtyards and a local market terrace.
Artisan Coast.town_city: Specialized quarters for glass, dyes, concrete, tile and galleries around a shared waterfront civic district.
Artisan Coast.port: Decorated quay, merchant workshops, sample halls and compact warehouses integrated into urban frontage.
Artisan Coast.fortress: Rare and decorative but functional sea wall/gate complex; defense is subordinated to urban life.
Artisan Coast.sacred: Patterned chapels, memorial courtyards and artisan guild shrines using the finest local decorative work.
Artisan Coast.industrial: Production remains workshop-scaled and visible from streets; dangerous furnaces get enclosed yards without becoming isolated factories.
Artisan Coast.ruin: Faded mosaics, broken colored glass, abandoned kilns and courtyards reused by newer artisans.
Artisan Coast.build_signature: Craft is visible at pedestrian scale; no blank industrial facades.

The Haunted Marches.circulation: Defended lanes, ditch crossings, wall gates and sightline-controlled paths.
The Haunted Marches.hamlet: Fortified farmhouse cluster with shutters, palisade, bell post and shared refuge cellar.
The Haunted Marches.village: Ring wall or palisade around chapel, hunter yard, storehouses and tightly packed homes.
The Haunted Marches.town_city: Layered defensive town with outer work yards, inner residential ring, ward towers and separated dangerous production compounds.
The Haunted Marches.port: Small guarded landing with chain gate, warehouse fort and watchtower rather than open waterfront.
The Haunted Marches.fortress: The purest regional expression: ditches, layered walls, ward towers, magazines and refuge halls.
The Haunted Marches.sacred: Ossuaries, grave chapels, memorial lantern roads and protected cemeteries.
The Haunted Marches.industrial: Hostile-mob systems are isolated by walls, drops, height or controlled corridors; worker housing remains outside hazard rings.
The Haunted Marches.ruin: Failed settlements are common: broken palisades, abandoned chapels and overgrown homes remain as warnings.
The Haunted Marches.build_signature: Everything communicates vigilance, fallback positions and survival memory.

The Blackfen.circulation: Boardwalk spines, ferry crossings, pole-marked channels and raised footbridges.
The Blackfen.hamlet: Three or four stilt homes, shared dock and raised storehouse on one boardwalk branch.
The Blackfen.village: Boardwalk market, ferry landing, shrine pavilion and craft sheds around a water junction.
The Blackfen.town_city: Network settlement with no single street grid: market platforms, council house, boatyards and neighborhoods occupy separate raised islands/platforms.
The Blackfen.port: Long boatsheds, shallow docks, ferry halls and cargo punts designed for channels rather than deepwater ships.
The Blackfen.fortress: Water itself is defense: narrow causeways, gate towers, floodgates and raised palisades.
The Blackfen.sacred: Pile-built cloisters, lantern walks, reed gardens and quiet water courts.
The Blackfen.industrial: Slime, herbs, reeds and wetland processing occupy open basins or raised sheds connected by washable walkways.
The Blackfen.ruin: Flooded foundations, drowned shrines and abandoned boardwalk pilings reveal old channel paths.
The Blackfen.build_signature: Settlement is a network floating over wetland rather than a town imposed on dry ground.

Stone Highlands.circulation: Stepped lanes, retaining terraces, quarry roads and heavy bridges.
Stone Highlands.hamlet: Dry-stone farm cluster tucked behind retaining walls with shared cistern and stone barn.
Stone Highlands.village: Quarry or pasture village with stepped square, masons' shed and deep-set houses.
Stone Highlands.town_city: Terraced quarry town with guildhall, cutting yards, bridge works, civic stairs and freight incline.
Stone Highlands.port: Deep stone quay, block cranes, warehouses and inclined haul road connecting high quarry terraces.
Stone Highlands.fortress: Low massive walls, gate tunnels and cliff-edge refuge structures; strength over height.
Stone Highlands.sacred: Austere mountain monastery-fort, hill shrine and refuge hall built from the same practical masonry.
Stone Highlands.industrial: Quarries and stone generation are open civic landscapes with cutting yards and transport systems, not hidden holes.
Stone Highlands.ruin: Old quarry faces, half-finished bridges, retaining walls and roofless stone halls remain almost permanent.
Stone Highlands.build_signature: Mass, terrace and permanence; buildings read as extensions of geology.

Red Clay Basin.circulation: Shaded arcades, courtyard chains, stepped mesa streets and aqueduct/canal routes.
Red Clay Basin.hamlet: Mud/brick courtyard compound around cistern, shade tree and drying yard.
Red Clay Basin.village: Shared kiln court, cistern plaza and shaded market lane organize low terracotta buildings.
Red Clay Basin.town_city: Layered mesa city with pottery quarter, water district, bazaar, courtyards and stepped civic terraces.
Red Clay Basin.port: Walled merchant court, terracotta warehouses, shaded cargo yards and controlled water storage.
Red Clay Basin.fortress: Thick earthen/brick walls, gate courts and cistern-protected refuge precincts.
Red Clay Basin.sacred: Stepped temple/shrine courts, water rituals and decorated kiln memorials.
Red Clay Basin.industrial: Kilns, clay pits, drying yards and glaze courts are grouped by fire/water needs and separated from housing by courtyards.
Red Clay Basin.ruin: Buried courtyards, broken cisterns, weathered terracotta walls and ancient kiln complexes.
Red Clay Basin.build_signature: Shade + courtyard + water storage + ceramic surface.

The Sunken Coast.circulation: Boat lanes, stilt walks, seawalls, tidal gates and raised causeways.
The Sunken Coast.hamlet: Low stilt houses around shared pier, fish shed and storm refuge.
The Sunken Coast.village: Tidal market deck, smoker sheds, boathouses and raised storehouse around protected lagoon.
The Sunken Coast.town_city: Lagoon city of connected quays, sea gates, elevated civic halls, tide mills and mixed dry/wet neighborhoods.
The Sunken Coast.port: Tidal basin, fish docks, salvage quay, tide gates and storm refuge define the settlement.
The Sunken Coast.fortress: Storm fort integrated with breakwater, lighthouse and channel controls.
The Sunken Coast.sacred: Waterline shrines, storm chapels and memorial bell towers marking drowned older towns.
The Sunken Coast.industrial: Kelp, fishing, drowned salvage and tidal processing extend into water; production landscape is amphibious.
The Sunken Coast.ruin: Submerged streets, broken sea walls and drowned foundations intentionally visible beneath newer settlement.
The Sunken Coast.build_signature: Old and new water levels are both legible in the built environment.

The Crystal Deep.circulation: Suspended bridges, carved galleries, lifts, vertical shafts and quiet restricted routes.
The Crystal Deep.hamlet: Small grotto enclave around one geode, garden or lift platform with carved rooms rather than freestanding houses.
The Crystal Deep.village: Cavern neighborhood linked by bridges around crystal garden, workshop or water court.
The Crystal Deep.town_city: Multi-level cavern city with research, transit, garden, residential and sealed sculk districts around monumental voids.
The Crystal Deep.port: No conventional port; gateway caverns and lift terminals perform the same exchange function.
The Crystal Deep.fortress: Controlled chokepoints, sealed gates and vertical access control rather than surface walls.
The Crystal Deep.sacred: Resonance observatories, crystal chapels, reflection pools and silent processional bridges.
The Crystal Deep.industrial: Amethyst/sculk/geology work frames natural formations and controls sound/light; machinery is secondary to cavern geometry.
The Crystal Deep.ruin: Pre-civilizational geometric complexes remain visually dominant; modern structures should look attached and temporary by comparison.
The Crystal Deep.build_signature: Void, bridge and carved geometry matter more than facade.

The Volcano.circulation: Heat-separated courtyards, basalt causeways, lava-channel crossings and heavy service roads.
The Volcano.hamlet: Worker compound around safe water/cooling court with thick basalt walls and protected roofs.
The Volcano.village: Forge village with communal furnace, cooling basin, storage vault and compact housing behind heat walls.
The Volcano.town_city: Caldera city divided into foundry, lava, craft, civic, port and residential heat zones.
The Volcano.port: Black-stone industrial harbor with cooling basin, fortress warehouses and heavy cranes.
The Volcano.fortress: Basalt citadel with protected cisterns, thick vaults and defensible causeways.
The Volcano.sacred: Forge shrines, memorial anvils and caldera overlooks rather than detached temple complexes.
The Volcano.industrial: Lava and foundry infrastructure is monumental but compartmentalized; heat management shapes every district boundary.
The Volcano.ruin: Solid basalt shells survive after roofs and machinery fail; old lava channels may cut through abandoned districts.

Pirate Island.circulation: Stacked alleys, rope bridges, cliff stairs, improvised docks and hidden tunnels.
Pirate Island.hamlet: Cove camp of reused ship parts, one tavern/store and hidden storage caves.
Pirate Island.village: Layered dock village with repair sheds, alehouse, market and lookout built from mismatched materials.
Pirate Island.town_city: Freeport accretes rather than plans: old fort, merchant blocks, tavern quarter, shipyard and newer additions overlap visibly.
Pirate Island.port: Dense stacked docks, dry docks, salvage yards, ropeways and warehouses with multiple unofficial entrances.
Pirate Island.fortress: Improvised citadel made from captured/reused structures, cliff geometry and overlapping defenses.
Pirate Island.sacred: Small sailors' shrines, memorial walls and repurposed foreign chapels rather than unified doctrine.
Pirate Island.industrial: Repair, salvage and contraband handling is distributed through yards, caves and docks.
Pirate Island.ruin: Ruins are usually reused immediately; surviving abandoned structures are inaccessible, cursed-by-reputation or strategically obsolete.
Pirate Island.build_signature: Visible layers of borrowed architecture without total stylistic unification.

The Ember Coast.circulation: Fortified causeways, portal courts, compartment gates and protected industrial corridors.
The Ember Coast.hamlet: Rare; a small portal-service fort with enclosed garden, barracks and resource yard.
The Ember Coast.village: Fortified work settlement organized around one Nether ecosystem and one safe portal/refuge court.
The Ember Coast.town_city: Separated district-city: portal administration, vegetation, gold/piglin, fortress mobs, magma/froglight, hoglin and stoneworks remain legible as different precincts.
The Ember Coast.port: Ash-coast freight fort with guarded portal/ship transfer, blackstone warehouses and controlled approaches.
The Ember Coast.fortress: Portal bastion with layered gates, refuge courts and high-risk containment districts.
The Ember Coast.sacred: Memorial courts for failed expeditions, guarded flame shrines and oath halls tied to safe passage.
The Ember Coast.industrial: Never one mega-factory. Each Nether production ecosystem gets its own fortified settlement language and buffer zone.
The Ember Coast.ruin: Abandoned portal courts and breached blackstone forts remain sealed or bypassed rather than casually repurposed.
The Ember Coast.build_signature: Compartmentalization and controlled risk define every settlement.

The Sapphire Coast.circulation: Water arches, stepped seawalls, reef paths, canals and ceremonial sea gates.
The Sapphire Coast.hamlet: Small pale-stone fishing/reef cluster with water court and low sea pavilion.
The Sapphire Coast.village: Reef garden, fish market, arched quay and neighborhood built partly over water.
The Sapphire Coast.town_city: Continuous land-water city with guardian district, reef gardens, merchant quays, towers and civic sea courts.
The Sapphire Coast.port: Formal arcaded harbor, customs tower, lighthouse, sail lofts and monumental entrance aligned to channels.
The Sapphire Coast.fortress: Sea gate complex and channel towers using water as both defense and civic spectacle.
The Sapphire Coast.sacred: Reef shrines, water courts and ceremonial marine monuments integrated with ecological stewardship.
The Sapphire Coast.industrial: Guardian/prismarine work is monumental but landscaped into reefs and water architecture rather than isolated.
The Sapphire Coast.ruin: Submerged pale-stone foundations and older sea gates become reef habitat and civic memory.
The Sapphire Coast.build_signature: No hard boundary between city and sea.

The Isles of Plenty.circulation: Shaded paths, veranda streets, farm tracks and open waterfront promenades.
The Isles of Plenty.hamlet: Open-sided homes, animal yard, orchard and shared shade pavilion.
The Isles of Plenty.village: Market pavilion, apiary/orchard courts, animal compounds and beach landing around lush green space.
The Isles of Plenty.town_city: Low open city with market pavilions, creature districts, tropical crop quarters and waterfront trade zone.
The Isles of Plenty.port: Colorful shaded quay, produce sheds, animal handling yards and breezy inns.
The Isles of Plenty.fortress: Minimal; storm shelter, watchtower and enclosed refuge compound rather than heavy fortification.
The Isles of Plenty.sacred: Grove shrines, garden courts and beach pavilions centered on abundance and stewardship.
The Isles of Plenty.industrial: Animal/crop production is broken into landscaped compounds separated by shade, gardens and paths.
The Isles of Plenty.ruin: Overgrown foundations and abandoned plantation walls disappear quickly under vegetation.
The Isles of Plenty.build_signature: Open shade and living landscape dominate over walls.

The Transit Isles.circulation: Platforms, concourses, ramps, bridges, ferry approaches and standardized wayfinding.
The Transit Isles.hamlet: Keeper settlement around one lighthouse, ferry, signal or repair function with an inn.
The Transit Isles.village: Crossroads settlement with station/ferry hall, lodging, repair, market and unmistakable route markers.
The Transit Isles.town_city: Interchange city where rail, ferry, freight, rockets and traveler services occupy separate but connected terminals.
The Transit Isles.port: Passenger/freight transfer first: covered piers, baggage halls, pilot offices, repair and lodging are organized for flow.
The Transit Isles.fortress: Route-control fort protects bridgehead, strait or emergency harbor while preserving clear civilian movement.
The Transit Isles.sacred: Travelers' memorials, route shrines and neutral halls rather than dominant religious institutions.
The Transit Isles.industrial: Transportation machinery is arranged around maintenance access and transfer, not manufacturing spectacle.
The Transit Isles.ruin: Obsolete stations, old route markers and abandoned bridgeheads document changing transportation eras.
The Transit Isles.build_signature: You always understand where to go next.

The Shrouded Isles.circulation: Long empty approaches, concealed paths, abrupt vertical transitions and hidden courtyards.
The Shrouded Isles.hamlet: Tiny isolated enclave with one strong silhouette, hidden entrance and more empty space than buildings.
The Shrouded Isles.village: Several separated compounds linked by subtle paths rather than a continuous street.
The Shrouded Isles.town_city: Sparse capital of distinct enclaves—observatory, storage vaults, Enderman court, research compounds—separated by deliberate wilderness.
The Shrouded Isles.port: Restricted arrival enclave with screening court, supply storage and hidden onward routes; no welcoming open harbor.
The Shrouded Isles.fortress: Concealed access, obsidian-like strongpoints, vertical traps/chokepoints and misleading outer silhouettes.
The Shrouded Isles.sacred: Observatories, silent courts and abstracted mainland ritual forms whose proportions feel subtly unfamiliar.
The Shrouded Isles.industrial: End production remains in separated compounds with large buffers; machines should never visually overwhelm mystery.
The Shrouded Isles.ruin: Some ruins should be ambiguous between abandoned mainland expedition sites and genuinely older End-influenced structures.
The Shrouded Isles.build_signature: Sparse composition, concealment and subtly alien proportion.
